title: Free AI sheet music maker: a tune to read and play · {name}
description: Ask for a tune and get its score: sheet music drawn in your browser and played note by note, to print or to save as MIDI. Free, nothing to install.
h1: Ask for a tune, and read it, hear it and print it.
acts: and read it, hear it and print it.
lede: Tell {name} what you want to play: a lullaby, a jig, the chords of a song, a warm-up for your choir. It writes the music as a score, drawn right in the answer, with a button to play it, each note lit as it sounds.
cta: Try it with a sample tune
try.ask: Write a lullaby for the piano in G major: eight bars in three time, with a simple left hand.
pane.title: A score written in {name}
demo.after: A lullaby in G, eight bars in three time: the right hand sings, the left holds one note a bar. Press {play} to hear it.
tune.title: Evening Lullaby
replay.title: One tune, step by step.
replay.why: The lullaby, from the request to the page on your music stand: what {name} read, what it worked out, and what you take away.
replay.reads: Your request: a piano, G major, three time, eight bars
{name}’s own skill “Music score”, which says how music is written down so that it can be drawn and played
replay.works: Composed eight bars: a melody for the right hand, one note a bar for the left
Checked that every bar adds up to three beats
Wrote it down in ABC notation, plain text that music software reads
replay.got: The score, drawn in the answer, with a button that plays it on the piano, a band gliding along as each note sounds.
replay.made: A MIDI file, made right here in this tab, to open in your notation or recording software. Or print the score alone, on a clean page.

io.title: What goes in. What comes out.
io.why: Say the style, the instrument and how long. A key, a tempo or a level help, and none is required.
io.ins: A style, a key, an instrument, how long and how hard
Pasted from a book of folk tunes, to draw, hear or change
Words to set to a melody, a syllable a note
io.outs: Drawn as sheet music, its lines broken to fit your screen
Played on the instruments it names, each note lit as it sounds
The score alone, ready for a music stand
To open in notation or recording software
exact.title: Written music, not a recording.
exact.why: {name} doesn’t generate audio. It writes notes: music you can read, check, change and play yourself.
exact.cards: A score as a musician reads one: staves, bars, keys, chords, and words under the notes. Every note is there to change.
The sound is made on your device, from the score itself, on the instruments it names. Offline the first time, it plays on a small synthesizer.
{name} composes, or writes out music in the public domain. Of a song still under copyright, it gives the chords or a short phrase, not the whole melody.
where.title: Where your music goes.
where.why: No {name} server keeps your request in a form it can read. What changes is the AI that answers, and you choose it.
where.cards: Your scores stay in your browser, encrypted. Nothing we can read reaches us.
Sent to the AI you chose
Your request and what you attach go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
The sound is made in this tab. The instruments are downloaded once, the first time a score plays, and your music is sent nowhere to be played.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. Without a sign-up, only the AI on this computer answers.
It writes notes, not sound files: no singing voice, no produced track, no MP3.
An AI composes by rule more than by ear: a tune can be correct and plain. Ask again, or change the notes yourself.
Of a song still under copyright you get the chords or a short phrase, never the whole melody.
{name} can be wrong: a bar may not add up, or a note may sit outside an instrument’s range. Play it through before a rehearsal.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for, or the AI on this computer, with no account at all.
Yes. Press {play} on the score: it plays on the piano, or on the instrument you asked for, each note lit as it sounds.
Yes. The score prints alone, on a clean page, and saves as an ABC or a MIDI file.
The piano unless you name another: violin, cello, flute, clarinet, trumpet, guitar, organ and many more, alone or together.
Can it write for several voices?
Yes: a melody with a bass, a piano’s two hands or a small ensemble, each on its own staff.
Does it work in my language?
Yes: titles and sung words are in yours. The notes read the same everywhere.
end.title: Try it with the lullaby.
end.why: The request opens in {name} and is answered at once, or as soon as you choose an AI. Then ask for your own tune.
